Panel Schedule — Six Circuits

What we do

Six services, done the way we'd want them done on our own place. If it's got wire running to it, it falls under one of these.

  1. 01

    Wiring

    New runs, rewires, and added circuits for homes, pole barns, and workshops — pulled clean, stapled straight, and labeled at the panel so the next person knows what they're looking at.

  2. 02

    200A Panel Upgrades

    Older Baldwin County homes weren't built for today's loads. A 200-amp service gives you room for the shop, the addition, and everything plugged in at once — without breakers tripping in the middle of supper.

  3. 03

    Repairs

    Dead outlets, flickering lights, a breaker that won't hold. We track it down to the actual cause, fix that, and don't sell you work you don't need.

  4. 04

    Installations

    Fixtures, shop and barn lighting, cabinet lighting — installed level, wired right, and tested before we pack up the ladder.

Circuit 05 — Emergency

Emergency Service

Power doesn't quit on a schedule, and down here a storm can knock a whole road dark. When it matters most, call.

Call (251) 200-6442
  1. 06

    New Construction

    From the meter base to the last outlet, we wire new homes and buildings across Baldwin County — rough-in through trim-out, working off your builder's schedule.

The Weaver Standard

Neat work isn't decoration — it's how the next electrician in that panel knows exactly what's what, and how you know the job was done by somebody who cared about it.

Why Weaver

The crew you'd want on your own place

Weaver Electric is Kevin Weaver's shop, out of Robertsdale — and the crew in that photo is Weaver Electric at work, two electricians with their heads down in an open panel on a real job. This is a local shop, not a franchise: the name on the truck is the name of the man who owns it.

That matters in Baldwin County. We wire the barns and shops people run their livelihoods out of, upgrade the panels in homes that have been in families for decades, and get called when a storm rolls through and the lights go out. The work has to hold up, because we live here too — we'll see you at the parts house, the ball field, and the grocery store.
